scope: Five visual concept boards for review, not production screenshots or verified project copy.

concepts.name: Typographic Studio
concepts.prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup.
Create ONE high-resolution landscape portfolio website design presentation image, approximately 3:2 ratio. It must look like an exceptionally well-art-directed, buildable website comp, not an AI mood board. This is concept exploration for a frontend / software / full-stack developer named Irabor. Start from a fresh identity, NOT the existing purple/pink dark monospace site. Present a large flat desktop homepage occupying roughly 76% of the board and a genuinely adapted narrow mobile homepage beside it, with consistent readable typography. Screens are front-on rectangular UI views, NOT laptops or phones photographed in perspective. Show enough page depth for selected work and the start of experience or about, not just a hero. Use short, carefully typeset English copy. Required useful content: "Irabor", "Frontend developer", "Work", "About", "Experience", "Résumé", and a clear contact action. Project names available: "Primewave Cleaning", "LGSC Election Results", "LugSpace", "PayShip". Product UI shown inside the project areas should be credible illustrative concept interfaces, not claims of actual production screenshots. No made-up employers, awards, client logos, user counts, business metrics, skill percentages, or availability status. No portraits or invented likeness of the developer. No stock bento cards, floating glass cards, gradient heading text, decorative 3D blobs, fake terminal windows, coding-rain backgrounds, skill icon clouds, or illegible lorem ipsum. Design specificity must come from hierarchy, proportion, imagery, rhythm, typography, and purposeful controls. Include subtle visible interaction affordances and a focused/active state. Avoid generic "I build digital experiences" marketing phrases. Outside the screens, only a small concept title at the top and a single small motion-direction note at the bottom. Desktop and mobile must belong to the SAME design; mobile must recompose rather than shrink. Crisp publication-quality UI and coherent spacing. Footer label outside the screens: "Concept exploration · Illustrative product screens".
CONCEPT TITLE: "01 / TYPOGRAPHIC STUDIO".
Art direction: vivid cobalt blue, warm white, and a disciplined vermilion accent. International typographic poster design translated into a personal developer portfolio. Large tightly set custom-feeling grotesk, bold rather than monospaced; exquisitely aligned small labels and hairline dividers. Main desktop is warm white with a very large cobalt "IRABOR" wordmark spanning the upper field, a small role beside it, and navigation integrated into the grid. Below, use a highly asymmetric editorial composition: a substantial blue image field showing an elegant conceptual election-results interface, with a narrow adjoining column for project title, contribution, and "View case study". A second smaller project strip creates a deliberate change of scale; an understated experience index begins at bottom. Enough whitespace to make the density intentional, never empty. Website looks like a serious independent typographic studio, not a SaaS landing page. Mobile has cropped-to-fit but fully readable oversized IRABOR typography, then one generous project cover with project context immediately beneath. One vermilion selected index marker, not rounded pill overload. Include an active project link underlined. Motion note: "Motion: project index changes the cover; type and navigation stay still."

CONCEPT TITLE: "02 / PRODUCT CINEMA".
Art direction: deep forest green almost-black, warm ivory text, and a sharp restrained chartreuse accent; rich photographic treatment of PRODUCT UI, no landscapes or random architecture. A cinematic portfolio designed around one beautifully presented product at a time. Header is small and confident. The first viewport is dominated by a wide dramatic crisp conceptual payment interface for PayShip, art-directed against a solid forest field. Place the title "PayShip" in immense refined contrasting serif type near the lower left of the dominant project stage, a small project description and role carefully aligned below, with a quiet vertical project selector on the opposite side. This is a product screening room, not a carousel of generic cards. Below the feature, show the beginning of the next project as a strong horizontal cut, with experience in a quiet typographic strip. Visual drama comes from scale, subtle edge light and solid color blocks, not bloom, neon, gradients, decorative spheres or glass. Mobile changes to a naturally scrolling full-width vertical feature with visible previous/next controls and readable caption. Do not hide navigation behind art. Motion note: "Motion: shared-image transition into a case study; manual navigation, no autoplay."

CONCEPT TITLE: "03 / ENGINEERING INDEX".
Art direction: sharply functional light-gray and off-white with graphite type and industrial burnt-orange details. A discerning software engineer's portfolio as a precise working index, with the graphic discipline of a technical publication, NOT a dashboard, NOT an IDE or terminal. Use a medium-height identity row: "Irabor" and "Frontend developer", concise personal description, small navigation, no gigantic marketing headline. Desktop topology is radically different from an image-led hero: dense refined left column of four project names, dates omitted if unknown, explicit category labels, a strong active row; large central product preview for Primewave Cleaning showing a credible schedule and assignment interface; right marginal notes explaining "Interface", "API boundary", and "Delivery". Below, a meticulous experience table and one small linked technical note. Use typography for functional metadata: mono only in technical labels and numbers, neo-grotesk for everything else. Light rules, square controls, measured typography, careful whitespace. This should feel like a designer-engineer's own elegantly constructed tool for understanding their work. Mobile becomes a short title and horizontally swipeable but button-labeled project index above the preview and concise notes; no microscopic columns. A fine burnt-orange outline marks the currently focused project selector. Motion note: "Motion: click a project to inspect its implementation; preserve focus and scroll position."
Project-domain accuracy: LugSpace is a student community platform, NOT coworking or workspace bookings. PayShip is a native MOBILE fintech payments app, NOT shipping or logistics. Avoid expanding the acronym LGSC. Do not invent personal work history or role claims.

CONCEPT TITLE: "04 / INDEPENDENT MAKER".
Art direction: expressive warm persimmon orange, ink navy, natural white and restrained lilac as a minor supporting color. Fresh independent creative-developer identity, confident and personal, with bold hand-tuned typographic composition and thoughtfully overlapping rectangular project sheets. NOT a collage of stickers, NOT childish doodles, NOT a standard centered hero. Desktop opens with a huge navy "Irabor." wordmark on a saturated orange field, aligned with a short visible "Frontend developer" descriptor and a compact navigation. The lower part of the opening field has an unusual but ordered project composition: two generously sized slightly offset sheets displaying coherent conceptual LugSpace community and Primewave service product interfaces, with clean label strips and a clear "Open project" affordance. A distinct off-white reading region begins below, containing a brief personal working statement and the start of Experience. The persona emerges through typography, color ownership, and small annotations about frontend craft, not fake photographs or motivational slogans. Use one carefully placed bracket annotation to signal the active project; avoid arbitrary rotation on all elements. Mobile is separately art-directed: wordmark and concise intro, then one full-width project sheet and the next partially visible below, conventional vertical scrolling, large touch control. Typography should be genuinely custom and editorial, not a default monospace or bubbly cartoon. Motion note: "Motion: project sheets settle into place once; direct touch and keyboard alternatives."
Project-domain accuracy: LugSpace is a STUDENT COMMUNITY platform, not coworking. PayShip is a mobile FINTECH PAYMENTS application, not shipping. Do not invent job dates or employers; the Experience section can show only its heading and a View résumé link. All copy beyond known identity and project names is conceptual placeholder copy.

CONCEPT TITLE: "05 / QUIET ARCHITECTURE".
Art direction: warm limestone white, true near-black, and a single disciplined oxblood accent. A highly refined contemporary architectural practice's portfolio grammar applied to a developer's work. Avoid beige generic blog appearance: make the typography spatial, huge, sharp and confident, using a very elegant high-contrast serif wordmark "Irabor" paired with tiny precise sans navigation. Desktop structure: a narrow persistent identity/navigation rail on the far left; a large cropped-to-edge but legible product-interface photograph-like artwork occupying the upper right, with "Primewave Cleaning" set in a quiet serif caption below, a very concise contribution statement, and the project number aligned on the outer margin. Below the first feature, a dramatically smaller second project in a disciplined offset position and a succinct chronological experience area. No card boxes, no rounded panels, no generic hero paragraph, no ornamental lines everywhere. It should feel authored, restrained, and collectible, with large intentional negative spaces balanced against dense precise typography. Product imagery is exceptionally crisp conceptual web UI, not literal building photos. Mobile replaces the rail with a thin header and brings the first project's label and image into immediate view, making work discoverable without an oversized intro. Oxblood used only in the selected navigation and one interaction cue. Motion note: "Motion: quiet image reveal and route continuity; normal scroll, instant reduced-motion mode."
Project-domain accuracy: LugSpace is a student community platform, PayShip is a native mobile fintech app, and Primewave Cleaning is a cleaning booking/operations platform. Do not invent employment dates or claims. Render Experience simply as a section heading and a link to the résumé, with no fabricated jobs. Product interfaces and supporting copy are clearly conceptual.
